inspection_summary: Verified the frozen 786-line normalized source line by line. The article develops quantitative Speiser-type zero correspondences for positive- and zero-degree extended Selberg functions, tests the mechanism on a parameterized family and the Davenport-Heilbronn function, and extends the comparison to imprimitive Dirichlet L-functions. Prose is coherent; displayed formulas have text-layer glyph loss but their roles are recoverable from adjacent prose, so formula-dependent units retain an explicit representation warning.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Functional-equation symmetry constrains migration without guaranteeing RH
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A Riemann-type functional equation enforces paired zero geometry and makes collision a gate for departure from the critical line, yet the same symmetry is compatible with infinitely many off-line zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The trajectory evidence is heuristic and the claim concerns the source's selected extended-Selberg examples, not arbitrary zeta-functions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Logarithmic-derivative negativity is the common counting interface
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across positive degree, degree zero, and imprimitive characters, sign control of the logarithmic derivative on vertical boundaries plus bounded horizontal argument change converts analytic structure into a zero-count comparison between a function and its derivative.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The analytic inputs and error scales differ: Gamma-factor growth yields O(log T), degree-zero finite structure yields O(1), and imprimitive transfer includes finite Euler factors.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Derivative zeros mark collision and can be detected by local contour moments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A multiple-zero collision forces a derivative zero, while argument-principle count and first-moment integrals provide a computational way to detect and locate such derivative zeros when direct root searches miss them.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source explicitly calls the Mathematica calculations heuristic and the extracted contour formulas require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite Euler factors act as a bounded perturbation of primitive Speiser behavior
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For an imprimitive Dirichlet L-function, the added finite Euler factors contribute a bounded logarithmic-derivative term, allowing the primitive ancestor's far-left sign control and contour argument to transfer while adding a deterministic zero-density contribution.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equality statement is conditional on RH for the primitive ancestor, and the source notes that analogous behavior is not supported for all functions lacking a Riemann-type functional equation.
